title: OpenClaw Day 1: Gateway, Session, and Control UI
summary: Fifteen-minute practice for naming Gateway, agent, session, and Control UI correctly, inspecting this WebChat without changing settings, and keeping updates/config owner-gated.
learning_objectives: Name Gateway, agent, session, and Control UI without mixing them up.
Describe the path from a WebChat message to an agent reply.
Keep install/update, config, and channel changes owner-run and out of this lab.

lessons.title: Four Parts, One Box
lessons.body: OpenClaw is a local Gateway that owns chat surfaces. The Control UI is the browser app the Gateway serves, usually on 127.0.0.1:18789. An agent is the model-plus-tools persona (here, Veritas Main). A session is one conversation's memory and tool loop. This WebChat is Control UI talking to the Gateway, which starts an agent run in this session.
key_points: Gateway: long-lived daemon; one per host; owns channels and the WebSocket API.
Control UI: browser dashboard served by that Gateway, not a second product.
Agent: who answers. Session: which thread they are answering in.
A clean training score does not approve config, updates, or new channels.

lessons.title: Day 1 Is Inspect-Only
lessons.body: Day 1 practice is look, name, and stop. You may open Control UI, read a session, and run read-only status. You do not patch openclaw.json, pair a new channel, or run openclaw update from this lab. Randall runs updates in a terminal or Control UI when he chooses. Completing this module is not that approval.
key_points: Live inspect: this chat, the session list, and `openclaw status` if needed.
Blocked here: config, auth, channels, pairing, plugins, runtime, and updates.
Message in, Gateway accepts a run, agent replies. That is the whole loop.

choices.text: The Gateway is the local long-lived process that owns channels, WebChat, and the Control UI WebSocket.
choices.feedback: Correct. One Gateway per host; Control UI and chats connect to it.

choices.text: The Gateway is the LLM vendor, such as xAI or OpenAI.
choices.feedback: Vendors supply models. The Gateway is the local OpenClaw daemon.

choices.text: The Gateway is this single chat thread and its transcript.
choices.feedback: That is a session. Many sessions can share one Gateway.

interactions.title: Who Runs Updates?
interactions.prompt: This training lab finishes with a passing score. What is still true?

choices.text: Randall still has to run `openclaw update` himself if he wants an update; the lab does not authorize it.
choices.feedback: Correct. Updates and config stay owner-gated.

choices.text: The agent should now run npm install -g openclaw and restart the Gateway.
choices.feedback: Agents must not install or restart the Gateway from training completion.

choices.text: A passing score lets the agent pair Telegram or Discord next.
choices.feedback: Channel pairing stays owner-gated and is not Day 1 work.

interactions.title: Day 1 Inspect-Only Minimums
interactions.prompt: Check every item that stays true for this lab.
checklist_items: I can name Gateway, Control UI, agent, and session.
This WebChat is Control UI talking to the local Gateway.
I will not change config, pairing, channels, or plugins from this lab.
I will not treat a training score as approval to update OpenClaw.

interactions.title: Day 1 Teaching Walkthrough
interactions.prompt: Watch the local teaching walkthrough, then mark it reviewed. You do not record anything.
interactions.capture_hint: Teaching walkthrough is embedded. You watch it; you do not record a clip.
interactions.caption: Watch-only map of Gateway, Control UI, agent, and session.

interactions.title: Day 1 Boundary Acknowledgement
interactions.prompt: Confirm this module is internal OpenClaw literacy only and does not approve Gateway updates, config edits, channel pairing, allowlist changes, or runtime mutation.
interactions.expected: I confirm this is internal OpenClaw Day 1 training only.
